newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK paper yields up,but little follow through trade.
newsitem.headline: HK paper yields up,but little follow through trade.

text.p: Hong Kong government paper yields jumped on Monday following the sharp fall in U.S. treasuries on Friday, but lacked follow through action, dealers said.
The seven-year Exchange Fund note yielded 7.85 percent versus 7.72 percent at Friday midday, five-year yielded 7.50 percent against 7.36 percent, and three-year 6.87 percent versus 6.76 percent.
The one-week bill yield jumped to 5.10 against 5.05 percent.
"Hong Kong followed the trend in the U.S. but there is not much follow through action," a dealer with a local bank said.
Players were still waiting for major economic indicators from the United States such as the employment figures due out on Friday, traders said.
On the interbank market, rates rose in line with buoyant expectations of the U.S. economy.
Overnight money was last traded at 5-7/15 3/8 against 5-1/2 percent, and three-month cash was last traded at 5-8/19 19/32 versus 5-5/8 percent.
